summary.one_liner: nvm is a per-user POSIX shell version manager that installs, switches between, and runs different Node.js versions from the command line.
summary.what_it_does: Installs Node.js and io.js versions into a per-user directory (default ~/.nvm) and switches the active version per shell with nvm use. Supports aliases such as default, node, and lts/*, plus a .nvmrc file so a project's version is picked up automatically. Commands include install, ls, ls-remote, exec, run, which, and uninstall. It can migrate global npm packages between versions with --reinstall-packages-from and reinstall-packages, and can install offline from cache. Binary mirrors can be set through environment variables, and it can fall back to compiling from source when no binary exists.
use_cases: switch between multiple Node.js versions per project
install a specific or latest LTS Node.js release
pin a project's Node version with .nvmrc
run a command under a chosen Node version without switching
install Node in Docker or CI images
install Node in air-gapped environments using cached downloads
notable: Works in any POSIX-compliant shell (sh, dash, ksh, zsh, bash) rather than requiring a separate binary
Reads .nvmrc files, including walking up parent directories
Supports LTS line aliases such as lts/* and lts/argon
Can reinstall global npm packages when moving to a new Node version
Environment-variable mirrors and unofficial-builds support for platforms without official binaries
caveats: Does not support Fish shell; alternatives are listed in the README
Windows support is via WSL, Git Bash, or Cygwin; native Windows is not supported
Platforms without binaries (for example FreeBSD) may need slow source compiles that require a C++ toolchain
